title_en: People's Procuratorate of Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province v. Liang Kecai et al. — robbery case
ruling_gist_en: The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Conviction of Illegal Detention for the Purpose of Collecting Debts Not Protected by Law provides that if an actor illegally detains or imprisons another person for the purpose of collecting debts not protected by law, such as usurious loans or gambling debts, he shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 238 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, the precondition for constituting the crime of illegal detention under the above-mentioned circumstances is the actual existence of debts not protected by law, such as usurious loans or gambling debts. Where an actor, merely on the subjective suspicion that the victim had set up a scam against him in a gambling game, illegally abducts the victim to recover gambling funds and forces the victim to hand over property, such conduct does not fall within the circumstances specified in the above judicial interpretation.

full_text_en:
Guangdong Province Zhaoqing City People's Procuratorate v.
Liang Kecai et al. — robbery case

Ruling Summary

The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Conviction of Acts of Illegally Detaining Others for the Purpose of Collecting Debts Not Protected by Law provides that where an actor illegally detains or confines another person for the purpose of collecting usury, gambling debts, or other debts not protected by law, the actor shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 238 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, a prerequisite for the crime of illegal detention under the above provision is the actual existence of debts such as usury, gambling debts, or other debts not protected by law. Where an actor merely subjectively suspects that the victim has set up a fraudulent scheme against him in a gambling game, and illegally seizes the victim and compels the victim to surrender property in order to recover gambling funds, such circumstances do not fall within the scope of the above judicial interpretation.

Pursuant to Article 263 of the Criminal Law, the crime of robbery is defined as the act of forcibly seizing public or private property by immediately using violence, coercion, or other methods against the owner or custodian of the property with the intent of unlawful possession. Where an actor immediately uses violence to control the victim and forces the victim to transfer money through online banking into an account designated by the actor, such conduct constitutes compelling the victim to surrender property on the spot, which satisfies the constitutive elements of the crime of robbery and shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 263 of the Criminal Law.

Procuratorial Authority: Guangdong Province Zhaoqing City People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Liang Kecai, also known as Liang Chuncai, male, 34 years old, farmer, residing at Nanshui Street, Guangning County, Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province. On December 7, 1994, he was sentenced by the Guangning County People's Court to three years' imprisonment, suspended for four years, for the crime of intentional injury. He was arrested in connection with this case on August 24, 2006.

Defendant: Liang Kezhi, male, 37 years old, Han ethnicity, secondary technical education, before his arrest was the owner of Huanan KTV in Guangning County, residing at Nanshui Street, Guangning County, Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province. On June 12, 2001, he was sentenced by the Guangning County People's Court to one year and four months' imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention, and was released upon completion of his sentence on June 27 of the same year. He was arrested in connection with this case on August 24, 2006.

The Guangdong Province Zhaoqing City People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution against the defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai for the crime of robbery before the Guangdong Province Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court.

The indictment alleged: Between May and July 2006, the defendant Liang Kezhi incurred huge gambling debts by participating in online "Baccarat" gambling, and therefore intended to kidnap the victim Pan Hanying to extort property. On the evening of July 28, 2006, Liang Kezhi conspired with the defendant Liang Kecai, agreeing that Liang Kecai would prepare ropes, adhesive tape, and other tools for the crime, awaiting an opportunity to act. At approximately 2:00 p.m. on August 3 of the same year, Liang Kezhi had previously booked Taizhu A Villa at the Bicui Lake Resort in Nanshui Street, Guangning County, Guangdong Province, and then under the pretext of transferring a power station, lured Pan Hanying to the villa. Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai jointly subdued Pan Hanying, bound and gagged him with ropes, adhesive tape, and other tools prepared in advance, and by violent means forced Pan Hanying to use his laptop to transfer RMB 545,000 via online banking to an account opened by Liang Kezhi at the Agricultural Bank of China. That afternoon, Liang Kezhi withdrew RMB 200,000 from the Agricultural Bank of China in three separate transactions. During the time Liang Kezhi was out withdrawing money, Pan Hanying seized the opportunity to resist, breaking free from the ropes binding his wrists. Upon discovering this, Liang Kecai strangled Pan Hanying with a rope, causing his death, and informed Liang Kezhi by telephone. Liang Kezhi then bought a fiber bag and rushed back to Taizhu A Villa, placing Pan Hanying's body inside. That night, Liang Kecai transported the body by van to a bamboo grove in Zhongzhou Village, Niuqi Village Committee, Gushui Town, Guangning County, where he buried it. The following morning, Liang Kezhi again withdrew RMB 345,000 from the Agricultural Bank of China.

In the early morning of August 8, 2006, the public security organs captured defendant Liang Kezhi. The following morning, defendant Liang Kecai surrendered to the public security organs.

On August 10, 2006, under the direction of defendant Liang Kecai, the public security organs unearthed the body of the victim Pan Hanying from the bamboo grove in Zhongzhou Village, Niuqi Village Committee, Gushui Town, Guangning County. Forensic autopsy determined that Pan Hanying died of mechanical asphyxia due to compression of the neck.

After the case was solved, the public security organs recovered RMB 445,440, HKD 510, a Toyota sedan (license plate: Yue AMH255), and a ring, and returned the Toyota sedan and ring to the family of the victim Pan Hanying.

In summary, the acts of defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai violated Article 263 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Criminal Law"). The facts of the crime were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and they should be held criminally liable for the crime of robbery. After committing the crime, Liang Kecai surrendered himself, and in accordance with Article 67 of the Criminal Law, he may be given a lighter punishment.

Defendant Liang Kezhi argued: He formed the idea of kidnapping Pan Hanying to recover money only because he suspected Pan Hanying had defrauded him through gambling, and did not have the intent to commit robbery. Afterwards, Liang Kezhi discarded all property on Pan Hanying's person, proving that he had no purpose of unlawful possession. The indictment's characterization of the defendant's crime as robbery was erroneous and should be found to be illegal detention.

Defense counsel for defendant Liang Kezhi argued: Liang Kezhi's conduct in this case constituted the crime of illegal detention rather than robbery for the following reasons: 1. The existing evidence submitted by the prosecutorial authority was insufficient to prove that Liang Kezhi had the criminal purpose of unlawfully possessing another person's property when committing the criminal act. Therefore, Liang Kezhi's conduct did not meet the constitutive elements of the crime of robbery under Article 263 of the Criminal Law and did not constitute robbery. 2. Liang Kezhi's conduct fell within the provisions of Article 238 of the Criminal Law and the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues concerning the Conviction of Acts of Illegally Detaining Others for the Purpose of Collecting Debts Not Protected by Law, and he should be prosecuted for the crime of illegal detention. 3. Liang Kezhi had a good attitude in admitting guilt and showed obvious remorse, requesting a lighter punishment.

Defendant Liang Kecai argued: His assistance to defendant Liang Kezhi in committing the alleged criminal acts was not for the purpose of unlawful possession, but to recover the money Liang Kezhi had been cheated out of by Pan Hanying. The two did not take any of Pan Hanying's property after the crime, and therefore did not constitute robbery.

Defense counsel for defendant Liang Kecai argued: Liang Kecai had circumstances warranting a lighter punishment in this case and should be given a lighter punishment for the following reasons: 1. Liang Kecai had no motive to rob the victim Pan Hanying. 2. Liang Kecai's killing of Pan Hanying constituted indirect intentional homicide; subjectively, Liang Kecai did not hope for or pursue the occurrence of Pan Hanying's death, and his subjective malice was relatively minor. 3. Liang Kecai surrendered after the crime and had a good attitude in admitting guilt, requesting a lighter punishment according to law.

The Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court found at first instance:

Between May and July 2006, the defendant Liang Kezhi incurred huge gambling debts by participating in online "Baccarat" gambling, and thus formed the intention to kidnap the victim Pan Hanying to extort property. On the evening of July 28, 2006, Liang Kezhi conspired with the defendant Liang Kecai, agreeing that Liang Kecai would prepare ropes, adhesive tape, and other tools for the crime, awaiting an opportunity to act. At approximately 2:00 p.m. on August 3 of the same year, Liang Kezhi had previously booked Taizhu A Villa at the Bicui Lake Resort in Nanshui Street, Guangning County, Guangdong Province, and then under the pretext of transferring a power station, lured Pan Hanying to the villa. Subsequently, Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai jointly subdued Pan Hanying, bound and gagged him with ropes, adhesive tape, and other tools prepared in advance, and by violent means forced Pan Hanying to use his laptop to transfer RMB 545,000 via online banking to an account opened by Liang Kezhi at the Agricultural Bank of China. That afternoon, Liang Kezhi withdrew RMB 200,000 from the Agricultural Bank of China in three separate transactions. During the time Liang Kezhi was out withdrawing money, Pan Hanying seized the opportunity to resist, breaking free from the ropes binding his wrists. Upon discovering this, Liang Kecai strangled Pan Hanying with a rope, causing his death. Liang Kecai then informed Liang Kezhi of this by telephone, and Liang Kezhi bought a fiber bag and rushed back to Taizhu A Villa, placing Pan Hanying's body inside. That night, Liang Kecai transported the body by van to a bamboo grove in Zhongzhou Village, Niuqi Village Committee, Gushui Town, Guangning County, where he buried it. The following morning, Liang Kezhi again withdrew RMB 345,000 from the Agricultural Bank of China.

In the early morning of August 8, 2006, the public security organs captured defendant Liang Kezhi. The following morning, defendant Liang Kecai surrendered to the public security organs.

On August 10, 2006, under the direction of defendant Liang Kecai, the public security organs unearthed the body of the victim Pan Hanying from the bamboo grove in Zhongzhou Village, Niuqi Village Committee, Gushui Town, Guangning County. Forensic autopsy determined that Pan Hanying died of mechanical asphyxia due to compression of the neck.

After the case was solved, the public security organs recovered RMB 445,440, HKD 510, a Toyota sedan (license plate: Yue AMH255), and a ring, and returned the Toyota sedan and ring to the family of the victim Pan Hanying.

The above facts were confirmed by the confessions of defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai, witness testimony, physical evidence, forensic DNA examination report, forensic autopsy report No. Ning Gong Xing Ji Fa Yi Shi Jian Zi (2006) No. 037 and photographs, scene investigation and examination records and photographs, records of the public security organs' capture of the defendants, billing statements and "check-in records" for the "Bicui Lake Resort Villa," search records and lists of seized items, on-site evidence collection records, explanations of the items collected, price appraisal conclusions, detailed records of account transactions for the account opened by Liang Kezhi at the Agricultural Bank of China on August 3, 2006, household registration materials, and other evidence.

The focus of the dispute at first instance in this case was whether the acts of defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai constituted the crime of illegal detention or the crime of robbery.

The Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

Pursuant to Article 263 of the Criminal Law, the crime of robbery refers to the act of forcibly seizing public or private property by immediately using violence, coercion, or other methods against the owner or custodian of the property with the intent of unlawful possession. This crime falls within the category of property crimes. Subjectively, it is characterized by direct intent and the purpose of unlawfully possessing public or private property. Objectively, it is characterized by the actor's immediate use of violence, coercion, or other methods of physical compulsion against the owner, custodian, or guardian of public or private property, promptly seizing the property or compelling the victim to immediately surrender property.

In this case, defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai and their defense counsel argued that the two defendants did not have the purpose of unlawfully possessing another person's property. However, based on the facts of this case, the two defendants, after prior planning, lured the victim Pan Hanying to the crime scene, controlled him, and demanded property. During the criminal process, they used violent means to force Pan Hanying to transfer RMB 545,000 via online banking into the account designated by Liang Kezhi. It is thus evident that the two defendants committed the alleged criminal acts precisely based on the purpose of seizing another person's property. Although this method of conduct differs from the general form of robbery where violence is immediately used to compel the victim to surrender property, once the victim's money was transferred into Liang Kezhi's account, it came under Liang Kezhi's complete control, and the result was essentially equivalent to the act of immediately using violence to seize property. Therefore, the conduct of the two defendants satisfied the constitutive elements of the crime of robbery.

With respect to the defense opinion of defendant Liang Kezhi and his defense counsel that Liang Kezhi was recovering gambling funds defrauded by the victim Pan Hanying rather than committing robbery, the court held that, pursuant to the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Conviction of Acts of Illegally Detaining Others for the Purpose of Collecting Debts Not Protected by Law, where an actor illegally detains or confines another person for the purpose of collecting usury, gambling debts, or other debts not protected by law, the actor shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 238 of the Criminal Law. A prerequisite for the crime of illegal detention under the above provision is the actual existence of debts such as usury, gambling debts, or other debts not protected by law. In this case, aside from the confessions of Liang Kezhi and defendant Liang Kecai, there was no evidence to prove that a debt not protected by law existed between Liang Kezhi and Pan Hanying, nor was there any evidence that Pan Hanying had set up a fraudulent scheme to defraud Liang Kezhi of property during gambling. Moreover, according to Liang Kezhi's confession, he only suspected that Pan Hanying had set up a fraudulent scheme in the gambling game to take his gambling funds. Therefore, the conduct of the two defendants in illegally seizing Pan Hanying and compelling him to surrender property did not fall within the circumstances provided for in the above judicial interpretation, and their conduct should not be convicted and punished as the crime of illegal detention. The defense reasons of Liang Kezhi and his defense counsel that his conduct constituted the crime of illegal detention were not established and were not adopted.

In summary, defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai, with the purpose of unlawful possession, used violent means to seize another person's property, and their conduct constituted the crime of robbery. The criminal circumstances were egregious, the consequences were serious, and they should be punished according to law. Liang Kezhi was the person who proposed the criminal intent and organized the others, played a principal role in the joint crime, and was a principal offender. Given that he had a good attitude in admitting guilt after his arrest, he could be given a lighter punishment. Liang Kecai used violence in the course of committing the joint crime, causing the death of the victim Pan Hanying. The criminal circumstances were egregious and the consequences were serious. Given that he surrendered after the crime and had a good attitude in admitting guilt, he could be given a lighter punishment according to law. The defense opinions of Liang Kecai and his defense counsel were adopted. The facts of the crime charged by the prosecutorial authority were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the charge was established, and should be supported.

Accordingly, the Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Articles 263, 36, 48, paragraph 1 of Article 56, paragraph 1 of Article 57, Article 64, Article 67, and Article 68 of the Criminal Law; Articles 119 and 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China; paragraphs 3 of Article 17, Article 27, Article 28, and Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Personal Injury Compensation; on August 15, 2007, rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Liang Kecai was convicted of robbery and sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, deprived of political rights for life, and subject to confiscation of all personal property.

2. Defendant Liang Kezhi was convicted of robbery and sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment, deprived of political rights for five years, and fined RMB 500,000.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, defendants Liang Kezhi and Liang Kecai did not appeal within the statutory period, and the prosecutorial authority did not file a protest. The judgment regarding Liang Kezhi became legally effective. The judgment of death with a two-year suspension of execution regarding Liang Kecai was submitted by the Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court to the Guangdong Province High People's Court for approval in accordance with the law.

The Guangdong Province High People's Court, upon review, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Guangdong Province High People's Court held upon review:

Defendant Liang Kecai, with the purpose of unlawful possession, jointly with the defendant at first instance Liang Kezhi, used violent means to seize another person's property, and his conduct constituted the crime of robbery. Liang Kecai used violence in the joint robbery crime, causing the death of the victim Pan Hanying. The criminal circumstances were egregious and the consequences were serious. According to law, he should have been sentenced to death, but given that he had the circumstance of surrender, he could be given a lighter punishment and sentenced to death with a two-year suspension of execution. The original trial judgment had clear findings of fact, reliable and sufficient evidence, accurate conviction, appropriate sentencing, and lawful trial procedures.

Accordingly, the Guangdong Province High People's Court, pursuant to Article 201 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Item (1) of Article 278 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on February 20, 2008, ruled as follows:

Approved the criminal judgment of the Zhaoqing City Intermediate People's Court (2007) Zhao Xing Chu Zi No. 25, convicting defendant Liang Kecai of robbery and sentencing him to death, with a two-year suspension of execution, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property.

This ruling shall take effect upon service.
